problems.stem: You are sketching the page list for a one-person portfolio site aimed at hiring managers. Which top-level navigation best matches that single audience and purpose?
options: Home, Blog, Photo Gallery, Fan Mail, Guestbook, Webring
index.html only, with every section stacked and no links
A single Downloads page that links to a 40 MB ZIP of everything
problems.explanation: A hiring-manager audience needs to reach evidence of your work fast: a short, predictable set of pages (About, Projects, Resume, Contact) maps directly to what they came to verify.

problems.stem: Your project page currently reads: 'Stuff I made.' Which heading is the strongest information-architecture revision for a reader scanning for relevant work?
options: Selected Projects: Data Dashboards and Web Builds
problems.explanation: A descriptive heading that names the category of work lets a scanner predict the content and decide to read on. 'Stuff' and 'Things' carry no orienting information.

problems.stem: You ask a current AI assistant (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude) to propose a sitemap. It returns Home, About, Services, Pricing, Team, Careers. What is the right next move for your personal student portfolio?
options: Adopt the full sitemap because the AI is more experienced at web design
Keep only the pages that fit a single-author student portfolio (drop Services, Pricing, Team, Careers) and justify the cut
Add even more pages so the site looks like a real company
Reject the whole idea of a sitemap because AI suggested it
problems.explanation: The AI proposal is a draft for a business, not a student. You judge it against your purpose and audience, keep the fitting pages, and document why you removed the rest.

problems.stem: A visitor lands on your Projects page from a search result. Which structure best supports their need to reach one specific project quickly?
options: One long page where all six projects run together with no headings or anchors
Each project as a card with a title, one-line summary, and a link to its own detail page
A page that auto-plays a slideshow of all projects with no way to pause
A page listing project titles only, with the details available by emailing you
problems.explanation: Cards with titles, summaries, and per-project links let a visitor scan, predict, and jump straight to the one project they want, which is the core job of information architecture.
